source.section: Dosage and Administration > Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder
source.note: Age 6+: start 5 mg once or twice daily; 'Only in rare cases will it be necessary to exceed a total of 40 mg per day'; extra doses 'at intervals of 4 to 6 hours'. Max 20 = 40 mg/day split in two (the label gives no per-dose max). The curve repeats doses round the clock; the label means 1-3 doses during the day.
d-amphetamine '9.77 to 11 hours' (l-isomer 11.5 to 13.8 h); d is 3/4 of the mix model = midpoint of the label range (curve value; change if you prefer another)

source.citation: de la Torre R et al. Clinical pharmacokinetics of amfetamine and related substances. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2004;43(3):157-85 (PMID 14871155)
source.note: Abstract: 'Their oral bioavailability is good, with a high distribution volume (4 L/kg)' (amfetamine-type stimulants as a class).
'peak plasma concentrations occurred approximately 3 hours post-dose'

source.citation: Widely repeated ~90% oral bioavailability figure for amphetamine (e.g. Wikipedia/Drugs.com), traced back to an unresolved citation tag ('handbook2022_PK') that could not be matched to an actual publication
source.note: No label, PK review (de la Torre 2004; Markowitz & Patrick 2017, paywalled), or database (DrugBank: 'Bioavailability data of dextroamphetamine is not readily available') gives a verifiable number -- not even an animal estimate. This is the weakest-sourced value in the dataset: a commonly repeated figure with no traceable primary source. Flagged for Anabella to replace if she finds a real citation.

source.section: Clinical Pharmacology > Pharmacokinetics > Metabolism and Excretion
source.note: At normal urine pH, 'approximately half' as alpha-hydroxy-amphetamine derivatives plus '30% to 40%' unchanged (0.5 + 0.35); very dependent on urine pH (1% to 75% unchanged). CYP2D6 is 'involved' but its importance is not stated, so no enzyme entry. (Oral bioavailability has its own weakly-sourced estimate in pk.bioavailability above -- see that field's source note for the caveat.)

journey.text: Absorbed from the gut; blood levels peak about 3 hours after a dose.
Boosts the brain chemicals dopamine and norepinephrine, which help with focus and attention.
Most of a dose leaves in urine, part unchanged and part broken down. Acidic urine speeds this up; alkaline urine slows it.
